requirements.name: cell count
requirements.datasheet: up to 18 cells. 'Using the LTC6813-1 with Fewer than 18 Cells': unused C inputs are shorted to the highest connected cell or left open, unused S pins are left unconnected, and unused inputs read 0.0 V (p. 85). TME needs V+ 16 to 90 V, V+ to C18 at least -0.3 V, C13 at least 2.5 V and C7 at least 1 V (p. 6). With V193's tie, C7 and C13 sit at the top cell, at least 2.8 V. Packs under 16 V (1 to 3 cells at 4.2 V, 1 to 5 cells at 2.8 V) need an auxiliary V+ of at least 16 V

requirements.name: isolation
requirements.required: monitor on the pack's negative; isoSPI or digital-isolator barrier rated 85 V DC working or more (V189)

requirements.name: tap current
requirements.required: at most 100 µA per tap pin powered and 10 µA unpowered, averaged over 1 s; the supply from top to bottom excluded (V190)
requirements.datasheet: C(n) leakage 10 nA typical, ±250 nA maximum when not measured. ±1 µA typical while measured (MEASURE state), no maximum given. 70 / 100 / 130 µA during open-wire detection only (p. 5). At 130 µA an open-wire check stays within 100 µA averaged over 1 s at a duty under 76 %. The figures are specified at V+ = 59.4 V. The C pin current with V+ under 16 V is not specified; that case is a pack under 16 V with the IO board unpowered

requirements.name: cell resolution

dropped_from_p3.reason: P3 is right that P2's reason does not hold. A fixed auxiliary V+ keeps the upper device at 11 V or more for any count, as rank 1's auxiliary supply does at 16 V. The stack fails V190 on the data sheet's maximums instead. With the IO board unpowered, the upper device's C12 must stay within MIN(V+ + 5.5 V, 75 V) (LTC6811-1/-2 Rev. C p. 3), so its V+ is fed from its own cells. Its V- sits on the split tap, so its supply current leaves the lead through that tap pin, and V190 excludes only the supply from top to bottom. IVP in SLEEP with VREG = 0 V is 4.1 µA typical, 7 µA maximum at 25 °C and 10 µA maximum over the full range (p. 6); the data sheet gives no maximum for 0 to 50 °C alone. The lower device's supply cannot cancel it, because no minimum is given. At least two more C pins join that tap: the upper device's C0 and the lower device's top used input. Each carries ±250 nA maximum when not measured (p. 5). Worst case 10 + 0.5 = 10.5 µA, over the 10 µA of V190. On typical figures (about 4.1 µA) it would pass. In the powered state the upper device also needs a floating auxiliary supply, which P3 names: from its cells it would draw 0.4 to 0.75 mA in REFUP or MEASURE (p. 6) through the split tap, against 100 µA. That floating supply needs its own 85 V barrier (V189). Source: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/LTC6811-1-6811-2.pdf, Rev. C, read by P3 2026-09-29T03:00:48Z and by P2 02:45:04Z, the same 4,362,021-byte file

report.value: worst case 10.5 µA on the split tap against V190's 10 µA: IVP SLEEP (VREG = 0 V) 10 µA maximum over the full range plus 2 × 250 nA C-pin leakage. Typical 4.1 µA. The 25 °C maximum is 7 µA; no maximum is given for 0 to 50 °C alone. LTC6804: 10 µA full range, 6 µA at 25 °C. LTC6812-1: 18 µA full range, 11 µA at 25 °C

with a fixed auxiliary V+ on the lower device, TME needs V+ at least C12 - 0.3 V and V+ - C6 at most 40 V (LTC6811 Rev. C p. 6). A 1-cell pack at 2.8 V gives V+ at most 42.8 V, and a full lower section of k cells at 4.2 V needs V+ at least 4.2 k - 0.3 V. So k is 10 cells or fewer, and the upper device holds 6 or more. A supply taken from the split tap would draw 0.4 to 0.75 mA through it (p. 6), against 100 µA
report.source: LTC6811-1/-2 Rev. C p. 6 (P3's copy, read 2026-09-29T03:00:48Z); V184, V190, V193; arithmetic
